ops.title: Delegation trap: a package with red dependencies gets zero compiler feedback — the phantom-completion machine
ops.body:
Found during fusekit's F4 holder migration (2026-08-03), after two lanes returned completion-shaped reports over an unchanged tree. The mechanism, proven with an injected-type-error probe: when a package imports siblings that fail at MODULE RESOLUTION (withdrawn imports), `go build ./pkg` stops before typechecking the package itself — a deliberate `var x int = "not an int"` in the target package never surfaces. So a lane assigned that package can write any amount of Go with zero compiler feedback, and the natural failure mode is a plausible report over unverifiable work.

Mitigations, in order of preference: (1) sequence or widen the lane so its dep closure compiles (fusekit's fix: yield the sibling types.go files carrying the shared contract to the blocked lane, compare-and-adopt against in-flight edits); (2) a throwaway typecheck island (stub the red deps to their design shapes in a scratch copy, migrate with feedback, land only the target package); (3) never accept a completion report for such a package without pasted gate counts — "the tree is the record" only works if the reporter CAN consult the tree's compiler.

Related orchestration rule that made the diagnosis possible: exit criteria as pasted command output, tree-fact checkers between stages, and checkback-with-evidence over report-without-diff.
